text:
samir: Quick sync request - I'm proposing a tiny refactor: consolidate multiple provenance headers into a single compact "cost token" that lives in the edge envelope. Motivation: duplicated lookups in ingest, inconsistent billing joins, and lots of ad-hoc heuristics.

mia: Sounds right. Can you sketch encoding? We need something that survives proxies and is cheap to parse.

samir: Plan: CBOR-lite payload, base62-encoded, versioned. Fields: v, tenant_id (tid), route_id (rid hashed), cohort (opt), flags (bitmask), sig (short HMAC). Example token (pseudo):
```
v1|tid:42|rid:3a7f|c:A|f:0x4|s:Qw9Z
```
Gateway decodes and writes into envelope as envelope.cost_token. Downstream services read from envelope metadata instead of re-hitting enrichment.

elaine: Two ops notes: 1) signing key management (rotate via KMS, support shadow keys) and 2) we should mark tokens with provenance confidence (trusted/untrusted) so billing can decide.

nina: How do we handle older SDKs and private deployments where we can't change the gateway?

samir: Fallbacks: SDKs can set the token when available (opt-in flag). For private/onprem, we'll ship an ingress transformer lambda that reads existing headers and synthesizes token. For older proxies that drop unknown headers, we can encode into existing allowed header or small cookie, but that's last resort.

mia: What about sampling? If tracing sampler drops body, token must be copied into the envelope before sample-dropping. Also ensure the runtime sampler doesn't prune the token.

elaine: Suggest adding a tiny invariant: envelope write happens pre-sampling and cost_token has a separate retention TTL independent of trace payload. That avoids losing attribution.

samir: Perf concerns: baseline token ~60-120 bytes depending on sig and optional metadata. Bench idea: measure median header overhead on HTTP/2 + gRPC framing. If >120 bytes it may hurt high-throughput endpoints.

nina: We should consider two token modes: dense (full fields) and packed (just tenant+route+sig) for high-QPS routes. Gateway picks based on route config.

samir: Good call. Also suggest trust strategy: if sig verification fails -> attach metadata costs.untrusted=true and kick async enrichment. Fail-open for latency, but metric heavily tagged.

elaine: For rollouts: phased approach - (A) infra + gateway decoder, (B) SDK opt-in, (C) ingress transformer for private, (D) ingest prefers token then falls back. Track mismatch rate, token-propagation rate, and untrusted fraction.

mia: Actionables:
- samir: prototype encoder/decoder and packed mode bench (this sprint)
- elaine: draft rollback/migration doc + KMS rotation plan (ETA Mon)
- nina: add observability counters (token.present, token.verified, token.untrusted, token.fallback-source) to gateway and ingest (ETA Wed)

ingest-bot: ci: gateway-token-proto build  tests OK :white_check_mark:

samir: I'll open a lightweight RFC once we have bench numbers. Thanks folks — want to avoid creating another long-lived header set.

mia: One more ask: include a small field indicating source: gateway|sdk|ingress so we can attribute accuracy by origin.

elaine: noted, will include in schema.

nina: ping me when the proto PR is ready, I'll wire metrics dashboards.

samir: will do. Sync at next eng-platform if anything blocks.
